title: How International IB Students Navigate US Deadlines
summary: A September-to-November plan for international IB students managing US deadlines, predicted grades, school forms, testing, and financial aid.
body_markdown:
Understanding how **international IB students navigate US application deadlines** starts with one essential fact: the United States has no single national undergraduate deadline. Each university sets its own dates, admission plans, testing rules, financial aid requirements, and document procedures.


For students seeking fall 2027 entry, September-November 2026 is the critical early-application period. You must coordinate essays, predicted grades, transcripts, recommendations, testing, financial documents, and school deadlines across several systems.


### The US application calendar at a glance


Most US universities offering **Early Action (EA)** or **Early Decision (ED)** set deadlines in November, commonly November 1 or November 15. Some institutions use different dates, so always verify the official page for your entry year.


Period Main priority


September Finalize the university list, confirm requirements, request school documents, and draft essays


Early October Complete the main application, testing plan, activities list, and financial aid preparation


Late October Proofread early applications and confirm counselor and teacher submissions


November 1-15 Submit many EA and ED applications, depending on each university's deadline


November 30 Submit the University of California application for fall 2027


December-January Complete Regular Decision applications and respond to portal requests


For fall 2027, the University of California application is open for preparation from August 1, with a filing period of **October 1-November 30** . UC uses its own application rather than the Common App, so it needs a separate workflow.


### Understand the admission plan before choosing a deadline


The deadline label affects what happens after admission. Do not select an early plan simply because it appears strategically advantageous.


Admission plan Is it binding? What it means


Early Decision Yes You normally commit to enroll if admitted and must withdraw other applications


Early Action No You receive a decision earlier without committing to enroll


Restrictive or Single-Choice Early Action Usually non-binding The university restricts some other early applications under its own rules


Regular Decision No You apply on the standard timeline and can compare offers


Rolling admission No Applications are reviewed over an extended period, sometimes until places fill


According to the[Common App application dictionary](https://www.commonapp.org/files/fy-toolkit/Resource_FYTR_AppDictionary_ENG_2025.06.24.pdf) , ED is binding, while standard EA is non-binding. International students needing substantial financial aid should examine ED carefully because it can limit opportunities to compare aid offers. Review the estimated cost, international aid policy, and agreement conditions before applying.


### Build one deadline matrix


A US application deadline is rarely just one date. Universities may set separate dates for admission, scholarships, financial aid, portfolios, testing, interviews, and supporting documents.


Create one row per university and record:


- Application platform, admission round, official deadline, and time zone
- Your school's earlier internal deadline
- Supplemental essays and program-specific requirements
- Transcript and predicted-grade procedure
- Recommendation requirements
- SAT, ACT, and English-proficiency policies
- Financial aid forms and deadlines
- Applicant portal status after submission


Common App states that applicants meet its deadlines by submitting by **11:59 p.m. in their local time zone** . Nevertheless, aim to submit at least 24-48 hours early to avoid payment, internet, or incomplete-section problems.


The[RevisionDojo global university application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-apply-to-university-as-an-ib-student-step-by-step-guide-for-global-admissions) recommends building internal buffers before official deadlines. A practical margin is **7-14 days** , especially when a counselor must approve or upload documents.


### Coordinate IB records with your school


Your application and school documents are separate parts of the process. Under the[Common App first-year process](https://www.commonapp.org/apply/first-year-students/) , counselors or authorized officials submit the School Report and transcript, while teachers submit recommendations when required.


Ask your counselor or IB coordinator in September:


1. Which school years appear on my transcript?
2. Will predicted IB grades be included, and in what format?
3. Will the school provide a profile explaining the IB and local grading system?
4. What is the internal deadline for November applications?
5. When will midyear grades and final IB results be sent?


Do not convert IB grades into a 4.0 GPA unless a university specifically instructs you to do so. The IB states that there is no standardized US conversion because institutions use different grading systems and may recalculate records using their own methods.


Predicted grades are school-generated forecasts, not final IB results. Procedures vary by school, and the IB does not impose one universal date for sending predictions to US universities. The guides to[IB predicted-grade timing](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-are-ib-predicted-grades-submitted-to-universities-what-every-student-needs-to-know) and[predicted grades for EA and ED](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-predicted-grades-early-decision-early-action) explain why students must follow their school's calendar.


### Follow a September-to-November plan


### September: verify requirements and request documents


Reduce your university list to a manageable set and verify every requirement on official admissions websites. Invite recommenders early, provide any information your school requests, and confirm whether your counselor can submit predicted grades.


Draft your activities list and main essay. CAS, the Extended Essay, leadership, employment, family responsibilities, and independent projects can provide evidence, but explain your contribution and development. The[RevisionDojo Extended Essay application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-i-use-my-ee-topic-in-college-applications) shows how to present your question, method, and intellectual growth.


### October: complete each university's requirements


Finish supplements and verify testing policies. A university may be test-required, test-optional, test-flexible, or test-free. English-proficiency rules are separate, and attending an English-medium IB school does not guarantee a waiver.


Open financial aid forms early. The CSS Profile becomes available on October 1, but institutions decide whether they accept it from international applicants and set their own deadlines. Universities may also request income documents, translations, financial certification, or institution-specific forms.


### November: submit and monitor


Submit each application before its deadline and save the confirmation. When portal instructions arrive, activate the account and check whether the university has matched your transcript, recommendations, test scores, and financial aid materials.


A missing item may still be processing. Wait for the university's stated processing period before asking your counselor to resend it.


### Handle final IB results separately


Most current IB students apply before receiving final Diploma Programme results. Universities therefore review transcripts, current courses, predictions when provided, and the rest of the application.


Final results are later sent through the IB's official transcript service. Current candidates normally arrange this through their DP coordinator. May-session results are released in July, while November-session results are released in December.


An uploaded screenshot is not an official result. The[IB transcript guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/support-students-transition-to-higher-education/requesting-and-sending-transcripts/) explains how results are sent directly to institutions electronically or on paper.


### Common fall-term mistakes


- Assuming every Common App university has the same deadline
- Confusing the university deadline with an earlier school deadline
- Applying ED without understanding the commitment or likely cost
- Assuming English-medium education guarantees a language-test waiver
- Converting IB grades to a GPA without instructions
- Forgetting scholarship, portfolio, or financial aid deadlines
- Waiting until November to request recommendations
- Submitting without checking the applicant portal


Protect both sides of your workload. Use fixed weekly application blocks while maintaining regular subject revision and coursework progress.


### Conclusion


International IB students navigate US deadlines successfully by treating the application as a coordinated set of timelines rather than one submission date. Confirm each university's rules, work backward from school deadlines, report IB records accurately, and allow time for testing, aid forms, and portal checks.


RevisionDojo can help you maintain academic progress while applications are demanding. Use[guidance on presenting the IB in US applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-in-college-apps-us) , then keep revision focused with Study Notes, Flashcards, the Questionbank, or Jojo AI.
